ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Law 23 of 27 April 2015 (AML/CFT), Executive Decree 363 of 2015, Law 25 of 12 June 1995 (Private Interest Foundations); Executive Decree 198 of 8 July 2021 and DGI Resolution 128-2021 (central final-beneficiary register and annual sworn declaration administered by the Dirección General de Ingresos); supervision by SSRF (non-financial sector) and STR filing to Unidad de Análisis Financiero; FATF Recommendations 24-25.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Founder identity documents: notarized certified copy of the founders passport (individual) or notarized copy of memorandum/articles and director register (corporate founder)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent notary public or corporate registry of the document country of origin
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (competent authority of the country of origin); Consular Legalization via a Panamanian consulate if the origin country is a non-Hague State

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing (Certificado de Existencia / Due Standing) of the corporate founder or of the foundations ultimate parent entity
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Home-country registrar of companies (e.g., UK Companies House; US state Secretary of State)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or Consular Legalization applicable to the issuing authority

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Special Power of Attorney granted to the Panamanian registered agent and to the foundations council members for incorporation and registry formalities
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary public of the country of origin or Panamanian notary upon foreign-signed document
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or Consular Legalization; Spanish certified translation required

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: KYC records of prospective foundation council members and protector: notarized passport copies, personal bank reference letter (dated within 90 days), and utility bill/residence proof
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Issuing bank and notary public of document origin
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarized original plus Hague Apostille or consular legalization when the agent's internal AML policy so requires

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: AML/CFT source-of-funds and source-of-wealth letter for the initial foundation endowment and for the green-coffee trade flows (beneficial-owner declaration)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Applicant founder, executed before a notary public, certified sworn translator where applicable
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarial attestation and, for foreign signatures, Hague Apostille or Consular Legalization

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Ley No. 25 de 12 de junio de 1995 (Private Interest Foundations Law), as amended, together with the applicable regulations of the Registro Público de Panamá governing private interest foundations
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registro Público de Panamá — Fundaciones de Interés Privado Section
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Escritura Pública de Constitución de Fundación de Interés Privado (Notarized Private Interest Foundation Deed)
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: Minimum statutory endowment of US$10,000 or equivalent value in assets; no escrow deposit requirement; the endowment may consist of cash, securities, or tangible property and must be precisely described in the foundation deed
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: FIRST BOARD (FOUNDATION COUNCIL) RESOLUTION — SPECIALTY GREEN COFFEE BEANS — adopted under Law 25 of 1995. The organizing founder and first council members resolve unanimously: (a) the foundation accepts the initial endowment of US$10,000 in cash; (b) the registered office is established at [Address], Panama; (c) the statutory purpose is international wholesale import, quality assessment, containerized distribution, and sale of single-origin green Arabica coffee beans; (d) the following officers are appointed: President, Secretary and Treasurer; and (e) the officers are jointly and severally empowered to complete Public Registry registration, open bank accounts, execute trade contracts, and engage legal counsel. Dated at Panama City, [Date].

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Notarization of Foundation Charter and Internal Regulations
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Instruct counsel to prepare the Spanish-language foundation deed; verify founder identification; execute the deed before a Panamanian notary; the notary seals and certifies original copies. The deed must state the foundation name, registered office, purpose, endowment, first council members, and any protectorship clauses.
required_dossiers: If founder is a legal person: certificate of good standing and power of attorney
Names, addresses and identification of first council members
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary or counsel identifies defects, draft and execute a rectification deed before the same notary; no re-filing is required if the registry has not yet received the dossier.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Panamanian Commercial Bank or Independent Appraiser
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Deposit or transfer not less than US$10,000 into a Panama-licensed bank account in the foundation's name, or set aside in-kind assets with an independent appraiser; obtain a banker's confirmation or certified valuation and retain the evidence for registry filing and compliance purposes.
required_dossiers: Certified assets appraisal if in-kind endowment
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registry questions value, obtain a supplemental confirmation or deposit the asset shortfall in cash to satisfy the endowment rule.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Registration with the Public Registry of Panama
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registro Público de Panamá — Fundaciones de Interés Privado Section
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the notarized foundation deed together with the endowment evidence and the registry cover sheet; pay the applicable official fee; await inscription in the Ficha Electrónica; once approved, the Public Registry issues the certificate of registered foundation.
required_dossiers: Original certified copy of the notarized foundation deed
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registry issues a defect notice (advertencia), file a written clarification within 15 business days, correct the omissions, and pay the re-examination fee; the foundation becomes effective with third parties only upon inscription.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Taxpayer Registration and Municipal Operating Permit
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI) and Municipio de Panamá / Local Municipality
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Apply at DGI for the foundation's tax identification (RUC) and at the municipality for the Aviso de Operación / commercial operating license; present the registered foundation certificate, lease or ownership evidence of the registered office, and identification of the local representative; undergo any municipal inspection required for the office or warehouse address.
required_dossiers: Certificate of registered foundation from Registro Público
Proof of registered address (lease or title)
Aviso de Operación application and fee payment
Fire safety certificate for the office or warehouse
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the municipality requires zoning or safety corrections, submit amended lease or site plans and a new fire clearance; appeal a denial to the Municipal Council within 10 business days.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not applicable for pure import and distribution activities; phytosanitary entry control is administered by the Ministerio de Desarrollo Agropecuario (MIDA) — Dirección Nacional de Sanidad Vegetal
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Commercial Operating License (Aviso de Operación) and, for each imported lot, Phytosanitary Import Permit (Permiso Fitosanitario de Importación); no industrial manufacturing operating permit is required

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt — no full EIA report; a simple environmental registration notice may be required if the covered warehouse or storage space exceeds applicable municipal thresholds
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No process wastewater or VOC-emitting coffee roasting operations; wastewater limited to sanitary use connected to an approved municipal system; solid waste including damaged green coffee bags must be consigned to authorized waste handlers and shipments must comply with applicable Panamanian environmental, phytosanitary and customs waste management rules

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety inspection and certification by the Panamanian Fire Department (Bomberos), structural load inspection for racking and mezzanine storage, occupational workplace clearance covering emergency evacuation plans, and a non-industrial occupancy certificate for the office and warehouse address

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI) of the Ministerio de Economía y Finanzas (MEF), Republic of Panama; digital taxpayer portal: DGI Virtual and SIF Electronic Invoicing Platform (https://dgi.mef.gob.pa); ancillary export clearance authority: Autoridad Nacional de Aduanas (ANA).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Step 1: The Private Interest Foundation (PIF), already recorded in the Public Registry of Panama with its resident agent and registered office, delivers its foundation charter (acta de constitución) and Registry certificate to the DGI through the resident agent. Step 2: The agent submits the RUC (Registro Único de Contribuyente) application in the DGI taxpayer registration module, attaching the foundation charter, Registry good-standing certificate, resident-agent appointment, and, where local economic activity exists, the Aviso de Operación and registered-office proof. Step 3: The DGI issues the RUC; the PIF is simultaneously enrolled for ITBMS where it performs taxable Panamanian-source activity, including coffee trading or domestic logistics. Step 4: If the PIF only holds protected assets and derives foreign-source income, it files a non-operation declaration (no Panamanian-source income) and submits zero/nil tax returns as required; foreign entities without Panamanian taxable activity are not obligated to obtain a Panamanian RUC.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Territorial_Scope — a PIF is a distinct legal person under Law 25 of 1995; Panamanian taxation reaches only income sourced within Panamanian territory. Foreign-source income, including most cross-border trading profits, falls outside the Panamanian tax base; an entity-level or pass-through layer is not superimposed unless the PIF conducts Panamanian-source commercial activity.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Panama does not operate a US-style check-the-box or hybrid-mismatch election regime. Available statutory and administrative elections: (i) registration as an active taxpayer versus a declarant of non-operation with no Panamanian-source income; (ii) election of the simplified small-taxpayer ('pequeño contribuyente') ITBMS regime for qualifying low-turnover local micro-retailers; (iii) election of the Sede de Empresas Multinacionales (SEM) preferential headquarter regime by qualifying multinational groups; and (iv) the standard territorial ISR regime, under which a PIF with no Panamanian-source income is not liable to income tax, while a PIF carrying local business is taxed at the standard corporate rate on Panamanian-source profits.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Impuesto de Transferencia de Bienes Muebles y Servicios (ITBMS) — Panama's value-added tax on the transfer of movable goods and the supply of services within Panamanian territory, supplemented by selective-consumption excise taxes (ISC) on designated goods.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: Panama imposes no general de minimis turnover threshold for ITBMS registration: any person performing taxable transfers of movable goods or taxable services within Panama must register for ITBMS and obtain a RUC upon commencing activity. A reduced 'pequeño contribuyente' simplified regime is available only to qualifying local micro-retailers with monthly turnover not exceeding approximately B/. 3,000 (annualized B/. 36,000), and is inapplicable to a wholesale green-coffee container distribution operation.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Panama operates a phased mandatory electronic-invoicing framework (Sistema de Facturación Electrónica — SIF) administered by the DGI. Registered taxpayers transmit each invoice in real time to the DGI through secured REST/SOAP APIs before issuance; the DGI validates the invoice and returns a unique authorization code ('código de autorización') with digital stamping, which the taxpayer renders as a QR element on the final invoice and simultaneously reports to the treasury platform. The mandate has been phased in by taxpayer category since 2022 (large, then medium, then small taxpayers); exporters must reconcile e-invoices with the SIGA customs declaration to substantiate the 0% ITBMS treatment. Unauthorized invoices lacking DGI clearance are legally ineffective and disallow input-credit claims.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Exports of tangible goods, including containerized specialty green coffee beans, are subject to ITBMS at 0%. The exporter must be a registered ITBMS taxpayer, be named as the shipper/consignor on the Panama customs export declaration (Declaración Única de Aduanas — DUA) filed through the SIGA/SISCOPE customs platform, physically remove the goods from Panamanian customs territory through an authorized port (e.g., Balboa or Cristóbal), and retain the bill of lading and payment evidence showing receipt from the non-resident buyer. Green coffee imported into Panama under a customs-suspension or transit regime and re-exported without being released for local consumption is not subject to import ITBMS, and the subsequent export is zero-rated; coffee cleared for local consumption and later exported carries ITBMS on the local purchase, with that input tax being creditable. Input ITBMS on domestic cost components (warehousing, inland freight, bagging, port handling) is creditable against output ITBMS, and excess credits are refundable by the DGI after cross-verification with customs records. Zero-rating is denied where the goods are consumed or diverted locally or where the documentation is incomplete, mismatched, or sham.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (Declaración Única de Aduanas — DUA) filed and validated through the Panamanian SIGA/SISCOPE customs system
Ocean Bill of Lading or Air Waybill evidencing physical departure of the containerized green coffee from Panamanian customs territory
Inward Remittance Certificate or SWIFT MT103 / documentary letter-of-credit settlement evidence crediting the export proceeds to the exporter's Panamanian bank account
Commercial invoice and packing list matching the DUA and transport document
Phytosanitary certificate issued by the Panamanian Ministry of Agricultural Development (MIDA) for green coffee bean lots where legally required
Container seal record and export weight/grade certificate evidencing the shipped green coffee quantity and quality
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Panama does not impose a standalone statutory foreign-exchange repatriation calendar; nevertheless, DGI export-zero-rating practice expects export proceeds to appear in the exporter's bank statements within 180 days of the DUA date, as reflected in the mandatory documentation bundle. Missing, diverted, or unrepatriated proceeds entitle the DGI to recharacterize the sale as a taxable local supply at 7% ITBMS, recompute output tax, and retrospectively claw back input credits previously claimed, adding statutory recargos, default interest (interés moratorio) per month of delay, and fines ranging from 50% to 100% of the evaded tax for erroneous or false documentation. Participating in sham export documentation (false DUA, phantom bill of lading, or unrepatriated proceeds) constitutes tax fraud under the Código Fiscal, exposing responsible officers, agents, and beneficiaries to criminal fines of up to USD 100,000 and imprisonment of up to five years. The DGI and the Autoridad Nacional de Aduanas (ANA) conduct joint retrospective audits, and the ordinary reassessment and clawback limitation period is generally five years from the filing of the pertinent tax return.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: No issuing central bank exists in Panama. Banking and FX supervision are vested in the Superintendency of Banks of Panama (SBP – Superintendencia de Bancos de Panamá); fiscal-agent and treasury functions are performed by Banco Nacional de Panamá under the permanent US-dollarization monetary regime (US Dollar legal tender; Balboa only a nominal coinage subdivision).
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Panama operates under full dollarization. Both current-account and capital-account transactions are freely convertible: there is no exchange-control law, no central-bank FX visa, no prior-approval requirement for inbound capital, and no restriction on outward remittances. Profit and endowment distributions to non-resident PIF beneficiaries are not subject to withholding tax or remittance approval under the territorial income-tax system; the only practical hurdles are SBP-mandated AML/KYC documentation and OFAC-compliant correspondent clearing.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: None. Panama imposes no statutory repatriation timeline, no mandatory surrender ratio, and no compulsory conversion of export proceeds. USD-denominated receipts from specialty green coffee sales may be retained in Panama or offshore at the foundation's discretion; only SBP record-keeping (minimum 5 years) and anti-money-laundering verification obligations apply.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: USD Operational Current Account and Trade Settlement (LC/Standby) Account
USD Operational Current Account with Commercial Letter of Credit Facility
Capital Escrow Account and USD Operational Account
Private Banking Operational Account for PIF Treasury
Capital Escrow / Custody Account and Trade Finance Account

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: LOW-MEDIUM. Under Decree-Law 9 of 1998 (as reformed by Decree-Law 2 of 2008), only SBP-licensed institutions may take deposits in Panama. An offshore digital EMI (e.g., UK FCA, Lithuanian, or Singapore-licensed) cannot open a Panamanian-domiciled USD account for the PIF, issue Panamanian clearing identifiers, or act as the principal settlement institution for coffee trade proceeds. EMIs may serve only as ancillary retail collection channels in EUR/GBP via local acquiring partners. An in-country alternative exists under Law 185 of 2021 (Financial Innovation Hub and SBP Sandbox), but the primary clearing rails must remain at an SBP-regulated Tier-1 bank.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Mandate: an in-person interview of at least one duly authorized person (a council member/director or the ultimate beneficial owner/founder of the PIF) is standard at SBP-regulated Tier-1 banks before account activation. The interview may be conducted virtually by a private-banking officer under SBP Accord 3-2016 only if the full CDD file is pre-certified by a correspondent bank and all documents are notarized and apostilled. Fully remote opening with zero physical verification and no apostilled Foundation Council resolution is not available for non-resident-owned PIFs.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Foundation opacity – final beneficiary concealed or only nominee directors presented without economic substance.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Complete beneficial-ownership chain (founder, council, protector, final beneficiaries) evidenced via the Foundation Charter (Acta de Fundación) and Regulations (Reglamento) filed with the Panamanian Registered Agent; SBP Accord 3-2016 CDD forms; professional reference letters from two SBP-regulated banks; apostilled corporate resolutions.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Source-of-funds opacity for the initial endowment (dotación) wired from a non-USD, high-risk or offshore-shielded jurisdiction.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: 12-month bank statements of the funding account; certified tax returns of the founder; notarized endowment/letter-of-gift; asset-sale or liquidation records supporting the transfer; confirmation the wire arrives as an OFAC-clean USD credit through US correspondents (Fedwire/CHIPS).

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Trade-flow mismatch – invoice/export origin country inconsistent with beneficiary bank jurisdiction or commodity risk profile.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Signed Specialty Green Coffee Trade Agreement; commercial invoice and packing list; clean-on-board bill of lading; phytosanitary certificate; roaster-level SCA (Specialty Coffee Association) contract form evidencing HS 0901.11 classification; UCP 600-compliant LC terms where applicable.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Exposure to perceived AML-sensitive coffee-origin countries (e.g., Ethiopia, Yemen, Myanmar) alongside standard Colombia/Brazil flows.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Enhanced Due Diligence file: supplier corporate KYC, OFAC/UN sanctions screening results, proof of physical commodity transit, blockchain-tracked original shipping documents, and legal-entity verification through the origin-country chamber of commerce or equivalent registry.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: PIF operating quasi-philanthropic distribution without clear commercial activity in ISIC 4631.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Charter clause expressly authorizing wholesale coffee distribution; management agreement with the resident agent; physical office or contracted logistics arrangements; vendor/customer contracts; annual audited financial statements; Panama ITBMS (VAT) registration if local procurement occurs.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Protocol: (a) the foreign founder or funding entity executes a SWIFT MT103 from a FATF- or US-regulated bank; (b) the USD credit is cleared via US correspondent channels (Fedwire/CHIPS) into the PIF's account at an SBP-regulated Panamanian bank; (c) SWIFT Field 70 must state 'Dotación de Capital – Ley 25 de 1995 – ISIC 4631 specialty green coffee trading' together with the foundation's registered name; (d) the foundation posts the contribution as an asiento de dotación in its asset register and updates the escrow records. No central-bank visa, exchange contract, or purpose-code declaration is required under Panama's dollarized regime; the SBP AML duty to retain source-of-funds evidence for at least 5 years applies.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Clearing rails selected by counterparty trust and ticket size: (1) SWIFT MT103 open-account USD payments to exporter banks for established suppliers in Colombia, Brazil, Central America, and Kenya; (2) irrevocable documentary Letters of Credit (MT700) issued by the Panamanian bank under UCP 600 for first-time or large-value (>USD 500,000) shipments, payable against original invoice, clean-on-board bill of lading, marine cargo insurance certificate, packing list, specialty-coffee origin certificate, and phytosanitary certificate referencing HS 0901.11; (3) documentary collections (MT400/DP-DA) as an intermediate trust-building tool. All disbursements are subject to OFAC sanctions screening of beneficiary institutions; Ethiopian birr (ETB) settlements are executed as USD-denominated payments (NDF-reference pricing) because the birr is non-convertible.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: OTC plain-vanilla FX forwards (EUR/USD, GBP/USD) under ISDA 2002 master agreements with SBP-licensed banks — permitted for hedging foundation funding and operating-currency exposure.

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) referencing Colombian peso (COP), Brazilian real (BRL), and Ethiopian birr (ETB) to hedge green-coffee purchase commitments in producer-country currencies without requiring onshore convertibility.
Cross-currency swaps (USD vs EUR/GBP/CHF) for long-term capital-call or escrow funding alignment, governed by ISDA/CSA documentation.
Vanilla European-style FX options (calls/puts) for asymmetric trade-commitment hedging; speculative option writing outside the PIF's treasury risk policy is not permissible.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Private Interest Foundation government fee (Impuesto Anual de Fundación de Interés Privado) - flat B/.750.00 annual charge, payment and regularization
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI), Ministerio de Economía y Finanzas (MEF), Republic of Panama
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: 1 January to 30 April of each calendar year under Article 19 of Law 25 of 1995, as amended by Law 41 of 2013; foundations are exempt from this fee during the first five years from the date of constitution
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: A 10% late surcharge plus statutory monthly default interest applies if payment is made after 30 April; failure to pay for three consecutive years authorizes the Registro Público to dissolve and strike off the foundation ex officio upon DGI notice; delinquent foundations are denied the Paz y Salvoconducto (good standing certificate) and cannot complete notarial or registry formalities

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Ultimate Beneficial Owner sworn declaration (Declaración Jurada Anual de Beneficiario Final) identifying founders, foundation council members, the protector (if appointed), and all beneficiaries or economic owners
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: DGI Beneficial Owner Registry (Registro de Beneficiarios Finales), electronic portal of the Ministerio de Economía y Finanzas, Panama
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually on or before 31 March for calendar-year filers (within 90 days after fiscal year-end); any change in shareholding, control, or beneficial ownership must be notified to the registry within 30 days from the date of the change under Law 129 of 2020 and its implementing regulations
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Administrative fines under the DGI formal-duty schedule, typically B/.250 to B/.50,000 depending on entity size and the gravity of the omission; suspension of the foundation's RUC; restriction of registry operations and certificates; the Panama resident agent remains jointly liable for persistent non-compliance

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual income tax return (Declaración Jurada de Renta) - required only if the foundation generates Panama-source taxable income, such as local resale or distribution of imported specialty green coffee; otherwise the territorial exemption applies and no taxable return is due
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: DGI (RUC electronic fiscal portal), Ministerio de Economía y Finanzas, Panama
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: On or before 31 March of the year following the fiscal year-end for calendar-year taxpayers; quarterly advance payments (anticipos) are due in the months of June, September, and December when the estimated annual tax liability exceeds the applicable statutory threshold
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: A 10% surcharge on the tax due for late filing plus statutory monthly default interest; fixed fines up to B/.5,000 for non-filing; suspension of the RUC; criminal tax-evasion liability for willful non-compliance or fraudulent returns

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Territorial exemption: foreign-source profit is not subject to Panamanian corporate income tax; no statutory tax holiday applies to domestic green-coffee distribution, so Panama-source trading income remains taxed at 25%; coffee export logistics subsidies may be available only upon registration with MIDA (Ministry of Agricultural Development) for qualifying agricultural export activities, but do not constitute a general CIT reduction.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Formulario 102 (Declaración Jurada de Impuesto sobre la Renta) for legal entities (Personas Jurídicas); filed online through the DGI e-Tax portal (www.dgi.gob.pa) under the taxpayer's RUC; paper filing is available for foreign taxpayers only with prior DGI authorization.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Within three months after the fiscal year-end (31 March for calendar-year taxpayers); no automatic extension; DGI may grant a one-month extension upon verified written application.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Ingresos brutos de fuente panameña (gross income from Panamanian sources)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report all Panama-derived turnover from green coffee bean distribution, including sales, commissions, and warehousing income; the PIF must allocate each Panama sale separately using its RUC and statutory accounting ledger.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Ingresos de fuente extranjera (foreign-source gross income)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Only income generated and economically completed outside Panama is excluded from taxable income; maintain bills of lading, certificates of origin, and sale contracts proving transfer of title and delivery outside Panama.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Costos y gastos deducibles (deductible costs and expenses)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Include ocean freight, marine insurance, customs duties, warehousing, and handling costs exclusively connected to Panama-source revenue; deductions require electronic invoices and bank transaction records in the name of the PIF.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Pérdidas de períodos anteriores compensadas (net operating losses carried forward)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Apply losses from the immediately preceding five tax years in chronological order; attach a loss schedule; the PIF cannot offset foreign-source income with Panamanian losses.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Impuesto sobre la renta determinado (computed corporate income tax liability)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Multiply net taxable income by 25%, apply quarterly advance payment credits, and remit any balance due with the return; overpayments may be credited to the following tax period.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing attracts a penalty of up to 10% of the tax due plus monthly late-payment interest of 1% (12% annual statutory rate) on the outstanding balance; non-filing enables DGI estimated assessment and an administrative fine of up to B/.100,000, with criminal liability for tax evasion where intentional.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 10% withholding on dividends paid out of profits that were subject to the 25% Panamanian CIT; 20% withholding on distributions funded from territorially exempt income such as foreign-source coffee trading profit or untaxed capital gains.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: A shareholder resident in a tax-treaty jurisdiction must submit a Certificate of Tax Residence (TRC) issued by the treaty country's revenue authority and endorsed by DGI, together with a treaty relief claim on Form 104, before the dividend payment date; the Panamanian payer must retain the approved relief certificate in its accounting file and may apply the reduced treaty rate only after DGI administrative approval; Panama's DTA network is limited and does not override territorial-source characterization of most distribution income.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory WHT: 12.5% on non-resident royalties and 6% on non-resident interest derived from Panamanian sources; treaty rates, where applicable in the limited Panama DTA network (notably Mexico, UAE, Qatar, Barbados, and Korea), generally range from 5% to 12.5% for royalties and 5% to 10% for interest, conditional on the beneficial owner producing a current TRC.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: B/.3,000,000 (US$3,000,000) in gross revenues during the tax period, or B/.1,000,000 (US$1,000,000) in cross-border related-party transactions; at or above these thresholds the PIF must prepare a Local File and, at group level, a Master File.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Panama ESR (Executive Decree 212 of 2020 as amended) classifies green coffee container distribution as a 'distribution and service center' relevant activity; a PIF with this scope must maintain in Panama a physical office, full-time employees, board minutes, a bank account, and annual operating expenditures commensurate with the value of the distribution activity; the annual ESR filing is submitted simultaneously with Form 102; absence of substance triggers penalties, loss of the DGI good-standing certificate, and potential deregistration.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Willfully omitting Panama-source coffee sales from Form 102, issuing false invoices, or executing back-to-back purchase contracts to shift profit to an offshore affiliate at below arm's-length prices.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Criminal Code Art. 280-A: imprisonment of 2 to 5 years and fines of 3 to 10 times the evaded tax; the tax administration additionally assesses unpaid tax with 12% annual interest and imposes a 10% penalty for an incorrect or late return; DGI may seal the warehouse and seize coffee inventory pending payment.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Foundation council members, officers, and the certified accountant who sign or design the fraudulent return are jointly and severally liable; Panamanian criminal courts may order preventive detention, travel bans (impedimento de salida), and civil restitution of the evaded tax; the corporate veil is pierced where the PIF is proven to be a mere façade.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating the green-coffee distribution PIF with only a registered office but no employees, lease, management presence, or Panamanian board activity; failing to file the ESR summary; routing transactions through a nominee council.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: ESR non-compliance carries fines of B/.50,000 to B/.1,000,000 for the entity; DGI may nullify tax registrations, deny refunds, and request the Public Registry to cancel the foundation's legal personality; repeat offense triggers immediate deregistration and a block on opening Panamanian bank accounts.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Foundation council members bear individual fines of up to B/.250,000 and may be disqualified from managing Panamanian companies for up to 5 years; the resident agent who fails to submit ESR reporting is also suspended and personally liable for penalties.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Money Laundering / AML Structural Red Flag
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Accepting cash or wire transfers from unrelated third parties for 'green coffee' without supporting trade documents; using the PIF to layer container payments among Panama, a low-tax jurisdiction, and a final buyer without economic rationale; failing to update beneficial-ownership records within 30 days of a change.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under Law 23 of 2015 and the Beneficial Ownership Registry, omission of BOI updates is administratively fined up to B/.1,000,000 per entity and B/.250,000 per responsible person; if the conduct constitutes money laundering, the Criminal Code imposes imprisonment of 5 to 12 years and confiscation of the full transaction value.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: All signatories and the resident agent face criminal prosecution; courts may issue freeze orders (embargo) on personal assets and prohibit departure from Panama; conviction results in permanent disqualification from acting as director, partner, or foundation council member in Panama.
